questions.q: What is the key difference between a classification and a sensitivity label?
options: A classification describes what kind of data something is; a sensitivity label describes how sensitive it is and can actively protect it
They are two names for exactly the same feature
Classifications only apply to files; sensitivity labels only apply to databases
Sensitivity labels are created during a scan; classifications are always manual
questions.explain: A classification is a logical tag describing the kind of data (like Credit Card Number). A sensitivity label describes how sensitive content is (Personal through Highly Confidential) and can apply real protection, like encryption or watermarks.

questions.q: Where are sensitivity labels created and managed?
options: In the Data Map's Annotation management section
In Microsoft Purview Information Protection, under Sensitivity labels
Only through PowerShell, with no portal option
Inside each individual scan rule set
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels are created and managed in Microsoft Purview Information Protection — a separate solution from the Data Map, though labels can extend into the Data Map.

questions.q: Why is a label's scope described as the single most important decision when creating it?
options: Scope has no real effect on the label
Scope only affects the label's color
Scope determines which settings you can configure and where the label is even selectable to users and services
Scope only matters for retention labels, not sensitivity labels
questions.explain: The scope you select (Files & other data assets, Emails, Meetings, Groups & sites) determines both which protection settings are available to configure and where the label becomes visible and selectable.

questions.q: Which scope must a sensitivity label have in order to reach assets in the Microsoft Purview Data Map?
options: Meetings
Groups & sites
Emails
Files & other data assets
questions.explain: A label needs the Files & other data assets scope to be available to Microsoft Purview Data Map — this scope also covers Microsoft Fabric, Azure, AWS, and other non-Microsoft-365 platforms.

questions.q: What has to happen before a sensitivity label is visible to any user or service?
options: Nothing — labels are visible the moment they're created
It must be published through a label policy
It must first be applied to at least one document manually
It must be converted into a classification
questions.explain: A label isn't visible to anyone until it's published through a label policy, which chooses which users and groups should see it and sets policy settings like default or mandatory labeling.
